verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The Lean fixes the two length scales as exact powers of q — radialLength q = q^{1/2}, axialLength q h = q^{1/2-h} — which is the paper's own later line on the same page (ℓ_r = q^{1/2}, ℓ_z = q^D, D = 1/2-h), not the comparability in τ displayed here. No declaration was found stating ℓ_r ≍ τ^{1/2}, ℓ_z ≍ τ^{1/2-h}, or the ratio ℓ_z/ℓ_r ≍ τ^{-h}; axialLength occurs in the whole repository only in Scaling.lean, in its definition and in core_axial_reynolds. The missing step is the passage from q to τ: tau_coordinate_identity gives τ = q(1-η²) exactly, so on |η| ≤ η_c one has (1-η_c²) q ≤ τ ≤ q, and raising this to the powers 1/2 and 1/2-h (both positive, since h < 1/100) gives the three displayed comparabilities with constants depending only on η_c and h. That composition is a few lines, but it is nowhere carried out, and the ratio ℓ_z/ℓ_r is never formed; core_radial_reynolds produces the same power q^{-h} from a different product (velocity × length), not from the ratio of lengths.
